'''Martin "Marty" Blume''' (January 13, 1932 – October 6, 2021) was an American physicist and [[editor-in-chief]] of the [[American Physical Society]]. 

== Early life ==
Martin Blume attended [[Abraham Lincoln High School (Brooklyn)|Abraham Lincoln High School]] in Brooklyn and studied physics at Princeton University.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 2022 |title=Martin Blume ’54 |url=https://paw.princeton.edu/memorial/martin-blume-54 |url-status= |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=Princeton Alumni Weekly |language=en}}</ref> He transferred to [[Harvard University]] for his master's degree, where he also received his doctorate in theoretical physics in 1959. 

== Career ==
After a research stay as a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Research Fellow]] at the [[University of Tokyo]], he joined the [[Atomic Energy Research Establishment]] in [[Harwell, Oxfordshire|Harwell]], UK, as a research scientist in 1960. In 1962, he moved to [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] in [[Upton, New York|Upton]], where he conducted research for over 30 years and served as deputy director from 1984 to 1996. At the same time, he was a professor of physics at the [[Stony Brook University]] from 1972 to 1980. From 1997 to 2007, he was editor-in-chief of the [[American Physical Society]]'s [[Physical Review]] series of journals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lazzaro |first=Kelly |date=5 November 2021 |title=In Memoriam: Martin Blume, Former Brookhaven Lab Deputy Director |url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=219233 |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=Brookhaven National Laboratory |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gibbs |first=Doon |last2=Lander |first2=Gerry |date=2022-05-18 |title=Martin “Marty” Blume (1932–2021) |url=https://doi.org/10.1080/10448632.2022.2035172 |journal=Neutron News |volume=33 |issue=1 |pages=13 |doi=10.1080/10448632.2022.2035172 |issn=1044-8632}}</ref> As editor-in-chief he was responsible, among other things, for converting the Physical Review journal series to digital editions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=American Physical Society |url=https://www.aps.org/archives/publications/apsnews/199804/blume.cfm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250513043723/https://www.aps.org/archives/publications/apsnews/199804/blume.cfm |archive-date=2025-05-13 |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
As a theoretical physicist, Martin Blume worked on [[neutron scattering]], [[magnetism]], [[magnetic resonance]], and [[synchrotron radiation]], among other things. He also played a leading role in establishing the [[National Synchrotron Light Source]] (NSLS) at Brookhaven National Laboratory, a facility that became an essential foundation for solid-state physics and materials science there.

== Personal life ==
He was married to Sheila B. Blume (née Bierman) and was the father of two children, Frederick and Janet. In his private life, he was interested in opera and classical music.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Martin Blume 1932 - 2021 |url=https://www.aps.org/archives/publications/apsnews/202112/blume.cfm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250210191104/https://www.aps.org/archives/publications/apsnews/202112/blume.cfm |archive-date=2025-02-10 |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=American Physical Society |language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==

* 1954: Shuichi Kusaka Memorial Prize in Physics<ref>{{Cite news |date=1954-06-15 |title=Princeton holds class day fete |work=The New York Times |pages=41}}</ref>
* 1981: [[Ernest Orlando Lawrence Award|Ernest-Orlando-Lawrence-Award]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-12-28 |title=LAWRENCE Martin Blume, 1981 |url=https://science.osti.gov/lawrence/Award-Laureates/1980s/blume |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=U.S. DOE Office of Science |language=en-US}}</ref>
* 1984: Member of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS)<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1984-07-27 |title=AAAS Members Elected as Fellows, 28 May 1984 |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.225.4660.388 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=225 |issue=4660 |pages=388–388 |doi=10.1126/science.225.4660.388 |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 1993: Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-10 |title=Martin Blume |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/martin-blume |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences |language=en}}</ref>
* 2003: Arthur H. Compton Award<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS UEC Arthur H. Compton Award - Past Winners |url=https://www.aps.anl.gov/About/Committees/APS-Users-Organization/Compton-Award/Past-Winners |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=Advanced Photon Source}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Blume is Co-Recipient of Compton Award |url=https://www.aps.org/archives/publications/apsnews/200306/blume.cfm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241212174744/https://www.aps.org/archives/publications/apsnews/200306/blume.cfm |archive-date=2024-12-12 |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=American Physical Society |language=en}}</ref>
* 2005: Meritorious Achievement Award des [[Council of Science Editors]]<ref>{{Cite news |last=Flanagin |first=Annette |date=2005 |title=Presentation to Martin Blume and Paul Ginsparg |url=https://csedev01.wpengine.com/wp-content/uploads/v28n5p147.pdfs |publisher=Science Editor |pages=147 |volume=28}}</ref>
